# Timba Contracts — Copilot Instructions

## Quick Orientation

- Anchor 0.32.1 program lives in `programs/timba/src`; TypeScript integration tests run from `tests/**/*.test.ts` via the single `anchor test` entrypoint.
- Program ID is `32Jr4JnXWvqq9GqPQynkooHsszaucUUvZfNLh2hdX2L5` (see `lib.rs` + `Anchor.toml`); update both plus any consumers after changes.
- Provider defaults to localnet with wallet `~/.config/solana/id.json`; dev tooling assumes Solana CLI + Anchor are already installed (devcontainer handles this automatically).
- Generated IDL lives in `target/idl/timba.json` and TypeScript types in `target/types/timba.ts`; other repos expect these to stay in sync.

## Core Architecture Patterns

- `lib.rs` re-exports instruction handlers that live under `programs/timba/src/instructions/`; each handler follows a strict Checks → Effects → Interactions flow (see `complete_game.rs`).
- Shared account constraints are centralized in `instructions/accounts.rs`; when adding fields or changing rules, adjust these constraints first to keep validation consistent.
- `state.rs` owns sizing constants (`ORACLE_SIZE`, `GAME_BASE_SIZE`, etc.) and serialization logic; update the size math and any derived tests whenever state layout changes.
- Player tracking relies on the canonical `participant_hashes: Vec<u64>` generated by `utils::participant_hash`; there is no bloom filter anymore, so keep this vector authoritative across Rust + TypeScript helpers.
- Winner selection uses `Game::calculate_winner_index` (secret key + last slot entropy); mirrored logic lives in `tests/test-helpers.ts/calculateWinnerIndex` and must stay byte-for-byte aligned when touched.

## Token & Oracle Handling

- PDAs use stable seeds: `b"oracle"`, `b"game"`, `b"game_token"`, `b"game_vault"`; any new PDA should reuse these conventions or document deviations.
- `GameTokenContext` wraps SPL CPI calls and supports both legacy and Token-2022 programs; always route new transfers through its helpers to preserve signer logic.
- Oracle configuration enforces fee %, timeout, and buffer ranges up front; exceeding limits should surface specific `ErrorCode`s so both contract and tests catch regressions.
- Game completion zeroes `total_amount` as the "already settled" sentinel; guard new logic against refilling this value post-completion.

## Testing Workflow

- Run the full suite with `anchor test` **once**; piping (`| grep`, `| tail`) or per-file runners (`bun test`, `ts-mocha tests/foo.ts`) are forbidden and break Anchor’s harness.
- Anchor triggers the `[scripts] test` command (a long-running `bun run ts-mocha ...`); expect ~8 minute runs and review complete logs for failures.
- Targeted tests require editing `Anchor.toml` `[[test]]` entries temporarily; revert before committing.
- `tests/test-helpers.ts` provides `TestEnvironment` and `TestUtils` for mint creation, player pools, oracle setup, deterministic randomness, and event capture—reuse these instead of re-implementing setup.
- When adjusting randomness, token math, or oracle timing, update the parallel helpers (`awaitBufferExpiry`, `calculateWinnerIndex`, etc.) so assertions remain truthful.

## Dev Commands & Conventions

- Build with `anchor build`; this regenerates the IDL/types consumed by tests and downstream services.
- After building, run `bun run update-idl` to copy the refreshed IDL into sibling `bot/` and `oracle/` packages (script in `scripts/update-idl.ts`).
- Lint/format TypeScript with `bun run lint` or `bun run lint:fix`; format Rust with `cargo fmt` (already enforced via repo guidelines).
- Keep code ASCII unless a file already uses Unicode; prefer descriptive comments only for non-obvious logic (matching existing style in `state.rs`).
- Do not revert workspace changes you didn’t author; coordinate with maintainers if unexpected diffs appear.
